text:
mike: Repro and heads-up: I hit a streaming generator goroutine leak in the Go SDK when cancelling the parent ctx while the SDK is mid-auth refresh. Small sample app attached below that reliably reproduces locally.

mike: ```go
// simplified repro
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
d := &fakeCreds{delay: 3 * time.Second}
client := NewClientWithCreds(d)

g, err := client.Generator(ctx, "x-model")
if err != nil { log.Fatalf("gen err: %v", err) }

// cancel shortly after starting
go func() { time.Sleep(150 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
stream, err := g.Stream(ctx)
if err != nil { log.Printf("stream start err: %v", err); return }
for chunk := range stream.Chan() { _ = chunk }
// goroutine stays blocked in repro until process exit
```

sarah: Thanks for the repro. Does the leak happen only when the credentials provider blocks (sync I/O) or also with slow network refresh?

mike: Both. In our case the provider does blocking I/O and doesn't accept cancellation so the handshake path can be stuck in token fetch. The stream loop never sees ctx.Done().

olga: Two UX-safe options we discussed: (A) make credential refresh API accept a ctx so callers can cancel refresh; (B) make Generator.Stream() register cancellation/select earlier and expose an explicit Abort() or Close() to forcibly tear down handshake.

james: For parity with other SDKs, I'd lean to adding `GetToken(ctx)` to the Go creds interface. Python/Node already require an explicit ctx/abortable refresh which avoids this.

kevin: Could we also add a handshake timeout in the client config with sane default (eg 5s) so sample apps don't deadlock on slow creds? That helps DX while we change the creds API.

mike: Agreed. Short-term: add handshake timeout config + update the onboarding sampleapp to show cancelling correctly. Long-term: change the creds interface and add compatibility shim (generator.Abort/Close) for existing users.

dev-bot: [ci-bot] E2E canary detected generator goroutine growth on main-private-e2e. Filed INF-3211: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3211

olga: Action items: 1) Update creds interface to include ctx param; 2) Add generator.Abort() as compatibility shim; 3) Add unit-test that simulates slow GetToken + ctx cancel and asserts no goroutine leak; 4) Add example snippet in sdk/onboarding README demonstrating correct cancel+timeout pattern.

james: I'll prototype the `GetToken(ctx context.Context)` change and include the Abort() shim in the same PR. Will add a sample-app commit and leak-detection test in CI.

mike: I'll update the onboarding README with a short example showing `context.WithTimeout` around handshake and how to call `g.Abort()` from another goroutine.

kevin: Also please add a small note in the CHANGELOG/compatibility doc explaining the creds API break and the shim for existing code. We should provide a migration snippet.

sarah: Sounds good. Moving to SDK parity triage for next sprint. Tagging @eng-ml for awareness in case model-serving infra wants to know.

mike: Thanks all. Leaving the repro in the devex thread — will paste a CI job link once the PR is up.
